sections.html:
Olathe holds the county courthouse for Johnson County, so the offices that record your deed and send your tax bill are in town. With 141,290 residents in 2020, it ranks fourth among Kansas cities.

Homeowners usually weigh three paths: list with an agent, sell on their own, or take a cash offer. Which one fits comes down to the shape the house is in and how fast you need the money. What follows covers the local rules and paperwork behind that decision.

sections.h2: Olathe code rules to clear before showing
sections.html:
Olathe's Community Enhancement Division inspects properties for exterior code violations. Walk your own yard with this list before the first showing.

  • Lawn and weeds have an eight inch ceiling.
  • Dead or diseased trees must come down, and limbs must stay above 13.5 feet over a street and 10 feet over a sidewalk.
  • Inoperable vehicles may not be stored outside, and tarps may not cover a vehicle.
  • Carts may sit at the curb only from 5 p.m. the evening before pickup until 5 p.m. the following day.

After a complaint, an officer inspects, notifies the owner and sets a time frame to comply. That time frame can be extended on request. If the owner still does nothing, the city can abate the problem or send a notice to appear in Municipal Court. If you have an open violation, fix it before closing so the buyer is not handed your problem.

Roofs, siding, gutters, doors and windows all fall under the exterior maintenance code. A badly aged roof worries buyers and can draw a city notice too.

sections.h2: Do you need a permit to replace a roof in Olathe?
sections.html:
Usually no. On single-family and duplex homes and townhomes, the city does not ask for a permit when you reroof or repair down to the roof deck. The work itself must still satisfy the current International Residential Code and Olathe's own code.

So an owner can swap out a tired roof before listing without waiting on the city. Save the contractor's invoice and warranty so a buyer can see what was done and when.

If your rental is enrolled in the city's automatic landlord utility transfer, call 913-971-9311 to cancel it once the house sells. Skip that call and utility accounts can keep landing back in your name.

Has the house been a short-term rental? Read any homeowners' association rules before telling a buyer that renting it out is fine. Hosts are expected to follow city noise, trash and property maintenance codes, and a new owner inherits the same duties.

sections.h2: Johnson County property taxes and appeals
sections.html:
An owner can settle the bill in one payment by December 20, or split it and pay the second half by May 10. Appraisal notices from the county appraiser are mailed by March 1. You contest a value first through an informal appeal, and the filing date is March 31 or earlier, 30 days after mailing under K.S.A. 79-1448.

Paying under protest runs on separate dates. Homeowners who pay directly file by December 20. When a lender escrows the taxes the date is January 31. Second-half or late full payments use May 10.

Selling with an appeal still open? Tell your closing agent early, so the protest paperwork follows the right person and the closing figures show what is really owed.

sections.h2: Recording a deed at the Register of Deeds
sections.html:
Your deed gets filed with the county Register of Deeds at 111 S. Cherry St., Suite 1200, in Olathe. Email and fax filings are refused. A mailed filing needs the signed original, payment and a stamped return envelope, and e-recording is open only to title companies and law offices already enrolled with the county.

A completed Kansas sales validation questionnaire goes behind the deed in the stack, and filing slows down when it is out of order. An exempt transfer needs its exemption number printed on the deed. The title company usually prepares all this. Your part is to supply legal names spelled as they appear on your present deed.

sections.h2: What to gather before you sell
sections.html:
Start a folder with your newest tax statement, the latest appraisal notice and any letter from the city's code staff. Drop in the roof invoice if you replaced the roof. Most early questions from buyers and title staff can be answered from that folder.

For a rental, add the lease and note when the utilities were moved or cancelled. If the house belongs to an estate, settle who has authority to sign before anyone books a closing.

sections.h2: How a sale moves from offer to closing
sections.html:
Once you accept an offer, a title company or closing attorney opens the file. They search the ownership record, look for liens and unpaid taxes, and prepare the deed and the sales validation questionnaire. Anything found in that search, such as an old lien or a misspelled name on the deed, gets sorted out before the closing date.

On closing day you sign the deed, and the title company sends it to the Johnson County Register of Deeds for recording. Property tax for the current year is split between you and the buyer, and any balance you owe is paid from your proceeds. Bring a photo ID, the keys and garage openers, and the name of your mortgage company if there is one so the payoff can be requested.

A traditional sale usually means cleaning, repairs, photos, showings, buyer inspections and a lender appraisal. Each step can stall the deal, and each one adds time. A cash buyer looks at the house once, makes an offer, and closes when you are ready.

You still get a title search and a proper closing. What you skip is the repair list, the open houses and the risk that a buyer's loan falls through at the last minute. If the city has sent a code notice, say so at the start. A clear picture of the house lets the buyer price it fairly and keeps surprises out of the closing.

sections.h2: When a cash sale makes sense in Olathe
sections.html:
Cash works well for a house with roof damage, a code notice, tenants or an estate behind it, and for owners facing a closing date no mortgage lender would hit. The buyer accepts the house as it stands, which means no repair list, no open houses and no waiting on a loan approval.

A tidy house and plenty of time can favor a listing, which may draw more bidders. Reach out with the address and we will say honestly which side yours lands on.

faqs.a: Johnson County. The city is its seat, and the appraiser, treasurer and register of deeds all work from offices in Olathe.

faqs.q: When are Johnson County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Pay all at once by December 20, or split the bill and send the second half by May 10 of the next year.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Olathe?
faqs.a: Not for a plain reroof or repairs down to the deck on houses, duplexes and townhomes. The code still applies to the work.

faqs.q: What is the Olathe weed height limit?
faqs.a: Eight inches. Owners must also keep up the right-of-way and easement strips next to their lot.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Olathe house with code violations?
faqs.a: Yes, as-is. An open city violation does affect a buyer, so either fix it first or tell us up front and we will account for it in our number.
